newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares show little sign of letting up steam.
newsitem.headline: German shares show little sign of letting up steam.

text.p: German shares showed little chance of giving up steam to reach more record levels after reaching another new high on Monday despite a weaker dollar.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 12.96 points at 3,575.37 points and was slightly lower at 3,569.10 points in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings on profit-taking.

A strong opening on Wall Street to the new week propelled the DAX index toward the psychologically-important 3,600 point level as the DAX traded up 59.93 points at 3,593.14 points in late IBIS computer dealings.
Two major DAX index heavyweights -- Deutsche Telekom and Deutsche Bank AG led the advance as the DAX ended bourse trade at a new record high in breaking the old mark at 3,568.28 points set on May 6.
Traders said the market may soon make a run for the all-time DAX high of 3,612.46 points but movements on Wall Street would play a key influence in any further advance.

The DAX received strength from Telekom, which surged to record levels on Monday as investors bet on upbeat earnings news from the newly listed German telecommunications giant, which holds its annual news conference on Tuesday.
Telekom shares led turnover through the day and hit an all-time high of 41.95 marks, a rise of 47 percent from its issue price last November of 28.50 marks a share.
The stock later ended bourse trade up 1.24 marks, or 3.2 percent, at 41.19 marks, far outpacing the DAX advance.
Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest commercial bank, also rose sharply, climbing 2.35 marks to 95.10 marks as traders cited technical factors for the gains.
Among other shares, camera maker Leica AG ended bourse trade down 6.80 marks at 43.50 marks after saying output delays would hurt its 1996/97 business year earnings.
Sportswear maker Puma AG led percentage decliners in post-bourse dealings, falling 3.45 percent, or down 1.90 marks at 53.10 marks, in moderate volumes.
